clue.text: More historic books probing a bit of North America are inside

indicators.note: the books are pushed into the coin, as a probe goes into something

parts.note: a dime is a small coin of the USA, literally a bit of North American money
OT, the Old Testament, whose books are older than the New Testament's

explanation.surface: A bibliophile poking into old volumes about America while staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of North America' looks like a place but is a coin. 'are inside' is slang for being in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To do time is to serve a prison sentence, so prisoners doing time are locked up inside.

clue.text: "Frigid" includes anything "well-ventilated"?

indicators.note: the word for frigid holds the other word within it

parts.note: dry can mean cold and unemotional, as a dry manner
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A dispute over whether a chilly room counts as nicely aired.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it read as a debate about labels; the question mark admits that well-ventilated is a kind way of putting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A room full of draughts (cold air currents, drafts in US spelling) is humorously described as being very well aired.

clue.text: The help being arranged to get a start-up in chat-room?

indicators.note: with 'in', the next pieces are got inside the rearranged letters
with 'to get', places the following pieces within
the letters of the help are put in a new order

parts.note: one can mean a, as in one day = a day
to boot a computer is to start it up

explanation.surface: Domestic staff are organised so a new company can be set up in an online forum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start-up' suggests a new company, but here it means booting a computer; 'a' is read as the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone kiosk is jokingly a small room where people go to talk, chatting down the line.

clue.text: Drink from Cup adorned with United cloak

indicators.note: read backwards in sense: the drink is decorated by the team's letters around it, so it sits inside them

parts.note: Man U is the common short name for Manchester United football club
tea is the drink typically taken from a cup

explanation.surface: A football trophy celebration: drinking from the Cup while Manchester United wear their capes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup' with a capital looks like a football trophy, but it is just the vessel tea comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteau is a loose cloak or mantle, a word borrowed from French for an outer garment.

clue.text: Scripture carved into holy building's architecture like this?

indicators.note: the scripture is cut into the building, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship
RE, religious education, the school lesson once called Scripture

explanation.surface: Sacred texts engraved into the stonework of a temple's design.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the holy building in the wordplay: Moorish design is the style of a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: Moresque describes Moorish style in art and building, the decoration typical of Islamic Spain.

clue.text: Initiate offers pot, being hidden in jumble

indicators.note: the three words are thrown together in a muddle and come out reordered

explanation.surface: Someone stashing cannabis in a heap of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiate offers' is the definition: to make the first bid at an auction or in a card game like bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the bidding means making the first bid, starting the round of offers at an auction or bridge table.

clue.text: The limits provided by context? Remarkable!

indicators.note: the answer is supplied by the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at how much context sets boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrema is the plural of extremum, a mathematical term for maximum and minimum values, the outermost points.

clue.text: Effecting rapid response, living with traction?

parts.note: quick means alive, as in the quick and the dead
a draw is a pull, so something being pulled along is on the draw, a whimsical phrase

explanation.surface: A medical note about a patient in traction who reacts fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living with traction' suggests a hospital bed; QUICK is the old sense of alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick on the draw reacts fast, originally a gunslinger fast to pull a pistol from the holster.

clue.text: Young flier upset about broken leg

indicators.note: the word for upset goes around the other letters

parts.note: to eat someone is to worry or upset them, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: the letters of leg are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A fledgling bird distressed by a fractured limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a baby eagle, a young bird that will soon fly.

clue.text: How "dot", as it were, transformed "tip"

indicators.note: these letters are changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a dot could, so to speak, turn into the tip of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' looks like the start of a question, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A word to the wise is a hint or piece of advice, offered to someone shrewd enough to heed it.

clue.text: Exhausted wife, away from work, grasps the essence of singleton sport

parts.note: all in means worn out
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the inner one

parts.note: resting is the actor's euphemism for being out of work

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is its core

explanation.surface: A tired wife on leave who has taken up a solo sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Actors between jobs are said to be resting; 'singleton' suggests a one-person sport but only gives its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in wrestling is a freestyle form of the combat sport with few holds barred.

clue.text: See 10
A pupil's most frequent yen, to break things up?

definitions.text: A pupil's most frequent yen, to break things up?

indicators.note: with 'up', the letters break into the word for things
with 'to break', the pieces split the outer word

parts.note: gear means belongings or equipment
P is the letter that occurs most often in pupil
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A school-leaver's strongest wish: to take time out and shake up their life.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a student's dearest wish to interrupt their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is time out between school and university, a pause many students long for.

clue.text: I'll get excited meeting Kirk — but not Ming

definitions.text: I'll get excited meeting Kirk — but not Ming

indicators.note: agitated letters move around into a new order
the letters of the following word are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A fan thrilled to meet Captain Kirk, but not the villain Ming the Merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirk is the Star Trek captain; Ming is Flash Gordon's foe, so the fan cares only for one franchise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trekkie is a devoted Star Trek fan who would be thrilled to meet Captain Kirk.

clue.text: How one conducted oneself in an emergency?

definitions.text: How one conducted oneself in an emergency?

parts.words: How one conducted oneself in an emergency?
parts.note: conducted is read as leading an orchestra: a stand-in conductor picked up the stick when needed

explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted oneself' suggests behaviour; read it as conducting music, done by someone who stepped in to wave the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up the baton means assuming a role or responsibility, literally picking up a conductor's stick.

clue.text: See 7
I'm estimating amounts among Acrosses, say, reading upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top
the answer lies among these letters

explanation.surface: A solver working through a crossword's across clues and estimating quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor values property or calculates sums due, such as tax or damages.

clue.text: Level with me from rear, I fasten filibeg — wrongly — in position

indicators.note: the whole is read from back to front
the pieces go inside the word for position

parts.note: to set is to place or position
to tie is to fasten
a filibeg is a kilt, the Highland skirt
ill means badly or wrongly, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A Scotsman putting on his kilt the wrong way round, asking for honest feedback.
explanation.walkthrough: S + ITIEKILTILL + ET gives SITIEKILTILLET, which reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To level with someone is to be frank with them, to speak plainly and honestly.

clue.text: Publicity given to unwilling PM's work

indicators.note: publicity's word is added on to the end of unwilling's

parts.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, reluctant
air means public exposure, as in giving views an airing

explanation.surface: A reluctant Prime Minister being pushed into the media spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM is Benjamin Disraeli, Victorian Prime Minister and novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothair is an 1870 novel written by Disraeli, a British prime minister.

clue.text: It's "times", then "add up", for prominent scholar

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to sum is to add

explanation.surface: A maths teacher's instructions: times, then add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was the great Dutch Renaissance humanist, one of Europe's most famous learned men.

clue.text: Order person from Prague, maybe, in proclamation?

indicators.note: a proclamation is spoken out, so the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: a Czech, as someone from Prague might be

explanation.surface: Someone declaring an edict while possibly being from Prague.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written instruction to a bank to pay money, a payment order.

clue.text: Colour coats not very regular

indicators.note: the colour covers the other phrase, surrounding it

parts.note: hue is a colour or shade
a bit means slightly, not very

explanation.surface: Paint applied unevenly, a colour that coats in an irregular way.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is a frequent visitor to a place, a regular customer.

clue.text: See 2
I'm unlikely to miss leader — naked — sitting in shade

indicators.note: the stripped word sits inside the word for shade

parts.note: dye is a colour or shade

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, its covering

explanation.surface: A naked boss lounging in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is an expert marksman, someone whose shots rarely fail to hit the target.

clue.text: Words Poirot and Hastings said Christie kept between them, perhaps

definitions.text: Words Poirot and Hastings said Christie kept between them, perhaps

parts.words: Words Poirot and Hastings said Christie kept between them, perhaps
parts.note: Agatha Christie put her characters' spoken words inside punctuation

explanation.walkthrough: 'kept between them' sounds like a secret between the detectives; it is the punctuation enclosing dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas surround direct speech, so the detectives' dialogue sits between a pair of them.

clue.text: See 24
Return a few minutes after three, Barking area connection

indicators.note: the turned word comes after the rearranged one
barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled
the word is turned back to front

parts.note: ten minutes is a few minutes

explanation.surface: A train timetable: departing a few minutes after three from Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired technology for a local area network connection.

clue.text: Intricate wordplay's free of old attempts to brainwash?

definitions.note: a noun for psychological warfare, which consists of such attempts

indicators.note: tangled letters are rearranged
the named letters are dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: Cryptic wordplay stripped of old tricks used for mind control.
explanation.definitionFit: Psywar is psychological warfare, propaganda campaigns meant to manipulate enemy minds.
